findings.notes: Percent-encoded dot-segments (%2e%2e) in a namespaced Policy apiCall urlPath bypassed the namespace clamp, letting a tenant POST cluster-scoped objects (for example MutatingWebhookConfigurations) as the Kyverno ServiceAccount and escalate to cluster admin; fixed by URL-decoding the path before normalizing and validating it (upstream 7ac176ac, on this branch as e58e1840d).

The same %2e%2e path-traversal in namespaced Policy apiCall urlPath let a tenant read resources in other namespaces with the Kyverno ServiceAccount; fixed by the same URL-decode-before-clamp hardening (upstream 7ac176ac, on this branch as e58e1840d).

The legacy apiCall service executor and the GlobalContextEntry external-API path skipped the SSRF host/CIDR blocklist and sent the scoped ServiceAccount token to arbitrary hosts; fixed by wiring the egress blocklist, redirect checks, and token gating into that executor (upstream #17234/#17299/#17310, on this branch as e090f5287, 7c148f984, and 3fdd28ede).

ImageValidatingPolicy ignored PolicyException.spec.images/allowedValues, so an exception meant for one image skipped signature verification for every image on a matched resource; fixed by refusing to treat a partial (image-scoped) exception as a full exemption (upstream #17307, on this branch as 9d19f4683).

The CEL globalcontext library was not namespace-confined, so a tenant-authored Namespaced*Policy could read cross-namespace GlobalContextEntry data; fixed by denying globalContext.* in namespaced policies at admission and runtime (upstream #17377, release-1.19 backport #17455 backported to this branch in PR #944).
